subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw adopt for stored gateway, channel, and provider secrets: native OS keychain, master-passphrase sealing, SecretRef-only migration, or a hybrid security-approved design?
rationale: Automation can identify the plaintext storage paths, but it cannot safely choose key custody, unattended service startup behavior, migration and rollback policy, recovery UX, or rotation guarantees for a credential security boundary.

options.title: Design native credential-at-rest encryption
options.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the mitigation
options.body: Document that transparent encryption is out of scope for now and focus on audit/configure/apply flows plus external ClawHub secret-manager resolvers.

options.title: Land partial auth-store sealing first
options.body: Use the open auth-store sealing work as a stepping stone while keeping this issue open for openclaw.json, backups, SQLite, and migration coverage.

recommendation.title: Design native credential-at-rest encryption
recommendation.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses repository product direction and the current auth persistence boundary that his recent refactor owns.
